\chapter{Review --- the Whole Present Tense}
\label{ch:spanish-review-present-complete}
\hlchaptermodality{32}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can produce all six present-tense forms of a regular -ar verb.}

The first complete paradigm in the book - withheld for thirty-two chapters until every box in it was earned.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[Practice]{Review — the whole thing, at last}

\label{lesson:ES-C07-repaso-presente-completo}



\begin{quote}
Nothing new in this chapter. Say \textquotedblleft{}we speak\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}they speak.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the table this book has been withholding}]
Six forms. Every one of them built separately, on its own, in its own lesson.

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{who} & \textbf{\emph{hablar} $\to$} \\
\midrule
yo & \textbf{hablo} \\
tú & \textbf{hablas} \\
él · ella · usted & \textbf{habla} \\
nosotros & \textbf{hablamos} \\
vosotros \emph{(Spain)} & \textbf{habláis} \\
ellos · ellas · ustedes & \textbf{hablan} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Most Spanish courses open with this table. This one has spent thirty-two chapters refusing to show it, because a table you cannot yet fill is a picture of work still to do, and a table you can fill is a picture of ground you hold.

Read it now and there should be no surprises in it. That is the point.

\textbf{And it is not one verb.} Every regular \emph{-ar} verb in Spanish — thousands of them — runs on these six endings, so this table is the present tense of a large part of the language.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item all six in order, top to bottom
  \item them out of order, as prompted: \emph{they} · \emph{we} · \emph{I} · \emph{a friend}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:} Until the whole set runs without a gap in it.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Give all six endings. (\textbf{-o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an}.) How many regular \emph{-ar} verbs does this fit? (\textbf{All of them}.) And why did the table wait until now? (Because every box in it had to be yours first.)
\end{tcolorbox}
